title: 第14回特定技能制度及び育成就労制度の基本方針及び分野別運用方針に関する有識者会議 議事要旨
key_claim: At its 14th meeting on 9 September 2026 the expert panel on the Specified Skilled Worker and Employment for Skill Development systems called the suspension of food-service intake, about two months after the Cabinet decision, an administrative mistake that surprised the market, and asked for advance notice, more frequent publication of intake numbers, a review of how caps are set, and examination of other fields expected to reach their limits. In aviation the Specified Skilled Worker projection would fall by 300 and the Employment for Skill Development projection rise by 300.
frame_summary: Shows the government's own expert panel treating the first sector cap suspension as a process failure and asking for the cap-setting rules to be reviewed before other fields hit their limits.

title: 令和８年６月末における在留外国人数について
date_evidence: Announced Friday 16 October 2026 by Justice Minister Takashi Yamashita (reported by Jiji Press on nippon.com, 16 October 2026); the agency page itself carries only the reference date 令和８年６月末
key_claim: Foreign residents numbered 4,281,026 at the end of June 2026, up 155,631 (3.8%) on the end of 2025. Specified Skilled Worker status stood at 444,256 (up 53,960; the 500,000 figure used as a disconfirming threshold in the scan is an analyst threshold, not a source figure), engineers and humanities specialists at 516,184 (up 40,394), technical interns at 457,509 (up 891).
frame_summary: Reports the end-June 2026 count of foreign residents as a record and breaks it down by residence status.

title: Japan's immigration politics starves restaurants of workers
date_evidence: Published 21 May 2026 (East Asia Forum); authors Naoto Higuchi, Sachi Takaya, Nanako Inaba
key_claim: Japan's restaurant industry suspended new Type 1 Specified Skilled Worker recruitment after reaching its quota of 50,000 in April 2026, with two weeks' notice; quotas rest on pandemic-era projections; the second-phase ceiling was raised to 820,000. Analyst calculation: 444,256 Specified Skilled Workers (Immigration Services Agency, end-June 2026) is 54% of 820,000; the 54% is not a source figure.
frame_summary: Argues that Japan's skilled-worker quotas were set from pandemic-era demand projections and that the political cost of raising them is now what starves restaurants of workers.
verbatim_quote: quotas remain based on pandemic-era projections that have proven far too low
verbatim_list: after reaching its quota of 50,000 migrant workers in April 2026
The suspension — announced with only two weeks’ notice — came as a shock.

title: Normalising foreign worker policies in Japan
date_evidence: Published 8 October 2026, East Asia Forum Quarterly Vol 18, No 3; author Midori Okabe, Sophia University
key_claim: Takaichi's immigration tightening is better seen as policy normalisation than a hawkish departure; successive governments have expanded admission of foreign workers while strengthening controls; the Employment for Skill Development Program was legislated in 2024 for implementation in April 2027.
frame_summary: Argues that Japan's tighter immigration politics continue a long pattern of expanding worker admission while strengthening control, not a sharp break.

title: Japan: debate begins on imposing a cap on the number of foreign nationals
date_evidence: 16 August 2026 (Il Sole 24 Ore, citing Asahi Shimbun reporting)
key_claim: The coalition agreement called for an overall cap, softened in the final text to quantitative management; a panel is to produce a framework policy by the end of the financial year that could for the first time include a cap.
frame_summary: Reports that Japan's ruling coalition is moving toward a numerical limit on foreign nationals, with the wording watered down to avoid conflict inside the LDP.
